newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras says EU wheat exports to rise, no target yet.
newsitem.headline: Legras says EU wheat exports to rise, no target yet.

text.p: The European Union will be able to increase its exports of soft wheat from last year's depressed levels in 1996/97 but has not so far drawn up a specific export target, Guy Legras, the European Commission's director general for agriculture, said on Wednesday.
In an interview, Legras said he thought soft wheat production would rise by 6.5 to 7.5 million tonnes in the 15-nation EU bloc this year, to 86 or 87 million tonnes.
This increase would be spread out between exports and some stock rebuilding "as appropriate," he said. He gave no figures.

He said that despite the likely return of EU export subsidies, following a fall in world prices, he did not see serious tensions between Europe and the United States over wheat sales, as in the days before a 1994 world trade accord.
Legras, who led the EU side in farm negotiations for the Uruguay Round global trade agreement, said such tensions were neither in Europe's nor the United States' interests.

Washington would in any case have a "moderate" wheat export policy this year because of a "middling" harvest, he predicted. The Uruguay Round limits subsidised grain exports until the turn of the century but has yet to be tested fully because of the rise in world grain prices in the past year.
But a collapse in prices to levels which marked the 1980s transatlantic subsidy war was unlikely, he said.
He pointed out that several eastern European countries which had hefty export surpluses last year have seen them vanish in 1996 due to disappointing crops. Some may need to import.
Uncertainties on the demand side included China's needs and the fate of some two million tonnes of wheat which might have gone to Iraq under an oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
The deal, allowing Baghdad to sell some oil for food and medicine, was frozen earlier this month after Iraqi army operations against rebel Kurds in the country's north.
